speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I see you are pregnant and experiencing vaginal bleeding with abdominal pain. To better understand your condition, how many weeks pregnant are you, and have you experienced any cramping or loss of fluid?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old woman, gravida 2, para 1, at 38 weeks' gestation. The patient reports experiencing vaginal bleeding for the past hour accompanied by severe abdominal pain. She mentions that she felt contractions before the onset of the bleeding, but the contractions ceased once the bleeding began. Her first childbirth was a cesarean section due to nonreassuring fetal heart rate.

speaker: Doctor
text: At 38 weeks with a prior cesarean section, this presentation raises concern for placenta accreta or uterine rupture. Have you noticed any changes in fetal movement, and is the bleeding bright red or dark? REQUEST TEST: Hemoglobin, Coagulation Profile, Type and Screen.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hemoglobin: 10.2 g/dL (decreased), Platelets: 200,000 /μL, PT: 11 seconds, aPTT: 30 seconds

speaker: Doctor
text: The lab results show mild anemia but normal clotting times. Given your history of a prior C-section, sudden cessation of contractions followed by severe pain and bleeding is highly concerning for uterine rupture or placental abruption. REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_Ultrasound, Fetal_Heart_Rate_Monitor. How many babies are you carrying, and is the fluid leaking from your vagina?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Vaginal bleeding. I also have Severe abdominal pain, History of contractions that stopped, Previous cesarean delivery.
